questions.group: Set 1 — Linear row (seven people, all facing north)
questions.context:
Seven friends — Karan, Lata, Manoj, Nisha, Omar, Priya and Rahul — sit in a straight row facing north. Positions are counted 1 (leftmost) to 7 (rightmost).

Clues:
1. Manoj sits exactly in the middle of the row.
2. Priya sits immediately to the left of Manoj.
3. Rahul sits at one of the extreme ends, and Omar sits immediately to the left of Rahul.
4. Nisha sits at an extreme end.
5. Exactly one person sits between Priya and Lata.
6. Karan does not sit at either extreme end.
questions.question: Who sits third from the left end?
questions.solution:
Left (1) to right (7), all facing north:

| Pos 1 | Pos 2 | Pos 3 | Pos 4 | Pos 5 | Pos 6 | Pos 7 |
|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|
| Nisha | Karan | Priya | Manoj | Lata  | Omar  | Rahul |

Deduction: Manoj is centre (pos 4); Priya immediately left → pos 3. Omar-then-Rahul must sit at the right end (Rahul needs a seat to his left), so Omar = 6, Rahul = 7. Nisha then takes the only free end, pos 1. One person between Priya (3) and Lata → Lata = 5 (pos 1 is taken). Karan fills pos 2, satisfying "not at an end."
questions.trick: In "north-facing" rows, left/right match the reader's own left/right, so pin the fixed anchor (the middle person) first, then attach the forced block (Omar–Rahul) to whichever end still allows a neighbour. Ends fill last.

questions.group: Set 2 — Circular table (eight people, all facing the centre)
questions.context:
Eight members — Amit, Bina, Chetan, Divya, Esha, Farhan, Gita and Harsh — sit around a circular table facing the centre.

Clues:
1. Divya sits immediately to the right of Amit.
2. Chetan sits third to the left of Amit.
3. Bina sits second to the right of Chetan.
4. Farhan sits immediately to the left of Bina.
5. Esha sits immediately to the left of Chetan.
6. Gita sits second to the left of Esha.
7. Harsh sits immediately to the right of Gita.
questions.question: Who sits second to the left of Harsh?
questions.solution:
Clockwise order around the table (all facing centre):

| Seat | Person |
|------|--------|
| 1 | Amit |
| 2 | Bina |
| 3 | Farhan |
| 4 | Chetan |
| 5 | Esha |
| 6 | Harsh |
| 7 | Gita |
| 8 | Divya |

Deduction (left = clockwise, right = anticlockwise): fix Amit; Divya is his right neighbour. Chetan third to Amit's left, Bina second to Chetan's right, Farhan on Bina's left, Esha on Chetan's left, Gita second to Esha's left, Harsh on Gita's right — each clue places one person, closing the circle uniquely.

two seats to Harsh's left: Gita then Divya
questions.trick: Write "facing centre → left is clockwise" at the top of your rough diagram. Then every "left" step moves clockwise and every "right" step anticlockwise, so you never flip direction mid-solve. "Second to the right" = skip one seat anticlockwise.

questions.group: Set 3 — Building floors with a favourite colour
questions.context:
A seven-storey building is numbered 1 (bottom) to 7 (top). Seven people — Ravi, Sonia, Tarun, Uma, Vikas, Wasim and Yash — live on different floors, and each likes a different colour: Red, Blue, Green, Pink, White, Black and Yellow.

Clues:
1. Sonia lives on floor 4, and she likes Red.
2. Uma lives on the topmost floor and likes Black.
3. Ravi lives immediately below Uma.
4. Two persons live between Sonia and Tarun, and Tarun lives below Sonia.
5. Yash lives immediately above Vikas.
6. Tarun likes Blue and Yash likes White.
7. The person who likes Green lives immediately above the person who likes Red.
8. The person who likes Yellow lives immediately below Uma.
questions.question: Who lives on the fifth floor?
questions.solution:
| Floor | Person | Colour |
|-------|--------|--------|
| 7 (top) | Uma | Black |
| 6 | Ravi | Yellow |
| 5 | Wasim | Green |
| 4 | Sonia | Red |
| 3 | Yash | White |
| 2 | Vikas | Pink |
| 1 (bottom) | Tarun | Blue |

Deduction: Sonia = 4, Uma = 7, Ravi = 6. "Two between Sonia and Tarun, Tarun below" → Tarun = 1. Yash immediately above Vikas: the only consecutive pair left in {2,3,5} is (2,3), so Vikas = 2, Yash = 3, leaving Wasim = 5. Colours: Green immediately above Red (floor 4) → Wasim (5) Green; Yellow immediately below Uma → Ravi (6) Yellow; the last colour, Pink, goes to Vikas.
questions.trick: Two-variable floor puzzles: lock every floor first using position clues, then overlay the attribute using "immediately above/below" links that hinge on an already-fixed floor (here Red on floor 4 fixes Green on floor 5). Assign the leftover attribute last.

questions.group: Set 4 — Month scheduling
questions.context:
Six people — Naina, Ovais, Puja, Qadir, Rekha and Sahil — go on vacation in six different months of the same year: January, February, April, July, September and November (not necessarily in that order).

Clues:
1. Puja travels in July.
2. Exactly one person travels between Puja and Naina, and Naina travels before Puja.
3. Ovais travels in the latest month among the six.
4. Qadir travels immediately before Ovais.
5. Sahil travels immediately before Puja.
6. Rekha travels in the earliest month among the six.
questions.question: Who travels in April?
questions.solution:
Earliest to latest:

| Order | Month | Person |
|-------|-------|--------|
| 1 | January | Rekha |
| 2 | February | Naina |
| 3 | April | Sahil |
| 4 | July | Puja |
| 5 | September | Qadir |
| 6 | November | Ovais |

Deduction: Puja = July (4). One person between Puja and Naina with Naina earlier → Naina = 2. Ovais latest → November (6); Qadir immediately before → September (5). Sahil immediately before Puja → April (3). Rekha, the earliest, takes January.
questions.trick: Convert months to a 1–6 timeline before reading clues; "travels before/after" then becomes simply "smaller/larger number," and "earliest/latest" nails down the two ends instantly.

questions.group: Set 5 — Stack of boxes
questions.context:
Seven boxes — P, Q, R, S, T, U and W — are stacked one above another. The bottom box is position 1 and the top box is position 7.

Clues:
1. Only two boxes are kept above box T.
2. Box W is kept immediately below box T.
3. Exactly two boxes are kept between box W and box S, and box S is kept below box W.
4. Box U is kept immediately above box S.
5. Box R is kept immediately above box U.
6. Box Q is kept at the top.
questions.question: Which box is at the bottom of the stack?
questions.solution:
| Position | Box |
|----------|-----|
| 7 (top) | Q |
| 6 | P |
| 5 | T |
| 4 | W |
| 3 | R |
| 2 | U |
| 1 (bottom) | S |

Deduction: "Only two boxes above T" → T = 5; W immediately below → W = 4. "Two boxes between W and S, S below" → S = 1. U immediately above S → 2; R immediately above U → 3. Q at top → 7, leaving P = 6.
questions.trick: "Only two boxes above X" fixes X directly (7 − 2 = position 5); count-from-the-named-end phrasing is the fastest anchor in stack puzzles. Build the rest as a chain of "immediately above/below" links.

questions.group: Set 6 — Days of the week
questions.context:
Seven people — Aarti, Bunty, Cyrus, Dev, Farah, Girish and Hema — attend a seminar on seven different days of the same week, from Monday to Sunday.

Clues:
1. Bunty attends on Thursday.
2. Exactly two people attend between Bunty and Girish, and Girish attends before Bunty.
3. Aarti attends immediately after Girish.
4. Farah attends on Sunday.
5. Cyrus attends immediately before Farah.
6. Dev attends immediately after Aarti.
7. Hema attends immediately after Bunty.
questions.question: Who attends on Wednesday?
questions.solution:
| Day | Person |
|-----|--------|
| Monday | Girish |
| Tuesday | Aarti |
| Wednesday | Dev |
| Thursday | Bunty |
| Friday | Hema |
| Saturday | Cyrus |
| Sunday | Farah |

Deduction: Bunty = Thursday (4). Two people between Bunty and Girish, Girish earlier → Girish = Monday (1). Aarti immediately after Girish → Tuesday (2); Dev immediately after Aarti → Wednesday (3). Farah = Sunday (7); Cyrus immediately before → Saturday (6). Hema immediately after Bunty → Friday (5).
questions.trick: Map Monday–Sunday to 1–7 and anchor the fixed day (Thursday) plus the "N-between" clue first — that clue usually has only one legal placement once you know the direction ("Girish attends before"). Then the immediate-after chain fills the rest in one sweep.
